text:
When it comes to budgeting and saving pots in the UK, the app-based digital banks are vastly superior to traditional high-street banks. 

The top three contenders are **Monzo**, **Starling Bank**, and **Chase UK**. Which one is "best" depends on whether you value automated budgeting, free utility (like paying bills from pots), or earning the best interest rate.

---

### 1. Monzo — *Best Overall for Budgeting & Visual Management*
Monzo essentially pioneered the concept of "Pots" and still offers the most comprehensive budgeting experience.

* **Pots Features:**
  * **Salary Sorter:** As soon as you get paid, a prompt lets you drag-and-drop portions of your salary into different pots (e.g., rent, groceries, holiday savings) and leave only your discretionary spending in your main balance.
  * **Bill Pots:** You can schedule Direct Debits and standing orders to come straight out of a specific pot, preventing you from accidentally spending bill money.
  * **Savings Interest:** Monzo connects to third-party banks in-app, allowing you to open easy-access or fixed-term savings pots that earn competitive market interest.
  * **Round-ups:** Rounds your spare change to the nearest pound and sends it into a pot automatically.
* **Budgeting Tools:** Excellent real-time spending breakdowns, notifications the second you spend, and monthly target budgets by category.
* **The Catch:** Some of the most powerful features—such as custom spending categories, auto-exporting to Google Sheets, and virtual cards linked directly to pots—are locked behind their paid tiers (*Monzo Extra* / *Perks* / *Max*).

---

### 2. Starling Bank — *Best Completely Free Experience*
Starling calls its pots **"Spaces"**, and unlike Monzo, almost all of its advanced features are **100% free** without any monthly subscription.

* **Spaces Features:**
  * **Bills Manager:** Direct Debits and standing orders can be assigned directly to a Space, so your bill money is separated from your day-to-day spending.
  * **Virtual Cards Linked to Spaces (Free):** You can create virtual cards (Apple/Google Pay or online) and tie them directly to a specific Space. For instance, you could have a "Groceries" space and tap with that virtual card so the money only comes from that space.
  * **Round-up Multiplier:** Rounds up purchases with optional 2x, 5x, or 10x multipliers to boost your savings faster.
* **Budgeting Tools:** The "Spending" tab automatically categorises your spending and gives clear pie charts and month-on-month trend comparisons.
* **The Catch:** It doesn't have an automated "Salary Sorter" like Monzo (you have to set up scheduled transfers into Spaces manually), and its savings interest rates are generally a bit lower than dedicated savings accounts.
